reasoning: The claim that the Great Wall of China is the only man-made structure visible from space with the naked eye is a well-documented myth. According to NASA and astronaut observations—including China's first astronaut, Yang Liwei—the Great Wall is generally invisible to the unaided human eye from low Earth orbit due to its narrow width (only a few meters wide) and materials that blend into the surrounding terrain. Furthermore, other man-made structures and features (such as large highways, city lights at night, dams, and mines like the Bingham Canyon Mine) are visible from low Earth orbit under appropriate conditions, making both parts of the claim entirely false.
